content.text: The text reviews pancreatic disease, including acute and chronic pancreatitis, carcinoma, fatty and amyloid degeneration, hemorrhage, duct obstruction, calculi, cysts, symptoms, diagnosis, and largely historical treatments. It then discusses acute, chronic, tuberculous, cancerous, localized, and infantile peritonitis: pathology, causes, clinical signs, complications, prognosis, ascites, and treatments—especially historical opium therapy. Ascites is linked chiefly to portal obstruction, cirrhosis, malignancy, and peritoneal disease; management includes diuretics, purgatives, sweating, nutrition, and paracentesis. Finally, tabes mesenterica is described as tuberculous mesenteric-gland disease, especially in children, causing abdominal distension, wasting, fever, digestive disturbance, and poor prognosis. Cases include a woman brought to her city home after travel, and a patient who went to Washington; these movements are explicitly noted.
